chatgpt-offline: ChatGPT can't work offline: every message goes to OpenAI's servers, on the website and in every app.
What does work offline is an AI that runs on your own computer: free apps like LM Studio, Jan, Ollama and GPT4All, OpenAI's own gpt-oss-20b, or GreenCube.
On a normal 8 GB laptop a local AI writes at about reading speed; with a gaming graphics card it's many times faster.
best-ai-for-students: There's no single best AI for students: ChatGPT Free for quick questions, NotebookLM for studying from your own notes with citations.
At university, Google's free year of AI Plus is worth claiming (it charges after the year unless you cancel).
For lots of PDFs, flashcards, pictures, offline study or notes you'd rather not upload, an AI on your own PC does the job, though it's slower on a laptop.
best-ai-for-lawyers: For research you can cite, use a tool tied to a legal database: CoCounsel (Westlaw), Lexis+ with Protégé, or Harvey at large firms.
General assistants like Microsoft Copilot or ChatGPT Enterprise are fine for drafting and summaries, but none is connected to a legal database.
When a matter's documents can't go to any cloud, a local AI on your own computer is the option. Whatever you use, check every citation yourself.
chatgpt-free-limits: Since August 2026, text chat on ChatGPT Free is unlimited.
What's still capped: file and PDF uploads, making pictures, voice and data analysis. OpenAI doesn't publish the exact numbers.
If you hit the limit in 2026, it's almost always because you sent a file, asked for a picture or used voice.
unlimited-ai: For text chat, ChatGPT Free has been unlimited since August 2026.
For files, PDFs, pictures and voice, every cloud AI we checked has a cap.
An AI on your own PC has no usage limits at all, because no server is counting. Your PC sets the speed.
best-offline-ai-chatbot: On a computer, LM Studio, Jan, Ollama and GPT4All are free and work offline once you've downloaded a model you pick yourself.
On a phone, PocketPal AI and Atomic Chat. Developers tend to use Ollama, llama.cpp or KoboldCpp.
Every one of them needs internet once, for the first download. All facts come from each app's own pages.
best-ai-for-researchers: Use one tool per stage: a search assistant tied to a real scholarly database to find papers, a citation map to see the field, a chatbot only for outlining and editing.
The test for any research tool: can you trace each claim back to the sentence it came from?
For unpublished data or drafts, add an assistant that runs on your own computer.
private-ai-assistant: The most private AI assistant runs on your own computer: your chats never reach anyone's server.
Of the 9 cloud assistants we checked, 5 train on your chats by default on a free personal account.
Turning training off helps, but your chats still travel to the company and may be kept for a while.
best-ai-desktop-apps: Cloud apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot) have the strongest models but need internet, and your chats go to the company.
Local apps (LM Studio, Jan, GPT4All, GreenCube) run on your PC: they work offline and keep your chats on your machine.
The newest cloud app on Windows is Gemini, launched on 10 September 2026.
is-local-ai-safe: Local AI is safe for most everyday use: your chats and files never reach someone else's server.
What matters more is what the AI may read and do. An app that only answers has little to lose; an agent that runs commands needs real limits.
The real risks are hidden instructions in files (prompt injection), plugins that run code, and model files from unknown uploaders.
pdfai-alternatives: First decide whether your PDFs can go to someone else's server.
If they can: ChatGPT and Claude for broad questions, NotebookLM for several sources, ChatPDF or AskYourPDF for one quick file.
If they can't: a tool that reads the file on your computer, like PDFgear for offline OCR or a local AI app for questions with the Wi-Fi off.
gemma-4-requirements: Gemma 4 E2B runs on an 8 GB laptop with no graphics card.
Gemma 4 E4B wants 16 GB of RAM, or any graphics card with 6 GB or more, where it's fast.
Gemma 4 12B needs at least 10 GB of VRAM. These numbers come from our own tests on 10 real PCs.
openwebui-alternatives: For a self-hosted chat page for a team, LibreChat is the closest swap; Onyx adds search across company documents.
For one person on one computer without Docker, LM Studio, Jan and text-generation-webui run the models themselves.
People mostly leave Open WebUI over its new licence, the setup (server, Docker, separate engine) or the fit.
